eyebrow: Earth and Weather · 地球與天氣
lead_en: Taiwan sits where two great plates meet and where typhoons pass in summer. Why does the ground shake? Where does the rain come from? Look inside the Earth, up into the sky, and down a river to the sea.
lead_zh: 台灣坐落在兩大板塊相接的地方，夏天又有颱風經過。地為什麼會搖？雨是從哪裡來的？往地球裡面看、往天空看，再順著河流一路看到海。

intro.en: Every lesson starts with something you have lived through: an earthquake alert on your phone, a typhoon day, a sudden afternoon storm. A 3D model shows what is going on, one idea at a time, and an English reading explains it, with Chinese a tap away.
intro.zh: 每一課都從你親身經歷過的事開始：手機上的地震警報、颱風天、突然下起來的午後雷陣雨。先用 3D 模型看清楚發生了什麼事，一課只講一個道理；再讀一篇英文短文把它說明白，中文翻譯隨點隨看。

intro.en: The lessons are grouped into four units: the ground beneath us, the sky above, water and the sea, and a changing Earth. When a lesson touches something already explained in Astronomy or How Things Work, such as the seasons, the tides, or rainbows, it links there instead of explaining it twice.
intro.zh: 課程分成四個單元：腳下的地、頭上的天、水與海、變動中的地球。遇到「天文教育」或「萬物原理」已經講過的東西，例如四季、潮汐、彩虹，就直接連過去，不重講一次。

intro.en: Every number is checked against a source listed at the bottom of each lesson, starting with Taiwan's own Central Weather Administration. What to do in an earthquake, a typhoon, or a thunderstorm follows official guidance only.
intro.zh: 每一個數字都查證過，出處列在每課最下方，並且優先採用中央氣象署的資料。地震、颱風、打雷時該怎麼做，一律只照官方的說明。

units.blurb_en: What is inside the Earth, why Taiwan shakes, how its mountains rose, and how a volcano erupts.
units.blurb_zh: 地球裡面有什麼、台灣為什麼會搖、山是怎麼升起來的，以及火山怎麼噴發。

lessons.title: What Is Inside the Earth?
lessons.blurb_en: The deepest hole people have ever drilled is about 12 kilometers deep. The center of the Earth is 6,371 kilometers down. So how do we know what is in between? Cut the Earth in half in 3D, travel down through its four layers, and see how earthquake waves show us what no one has ever seen.
lessons.blurb_zh: 人類鑽過最深的洞，大約 12 公里深。地球的中心在 6,371 公里底下。那麼中間有什麼，我們是怎麼知道的？在 3D 裡把地球切成兩半，一路往下穿過四層，再看看地震波怎麼讓我們「看見」從來沒有人看過的地方。
lessons.big_idea_en: The Earth has four layers. On the outside is a thin, hard crust. Under it is the mantle, thick and solid but able to flow very slowly. Deeper still is the outer core, made of liquid iron and nickel, and at the center is the inner core, a solid ball of iron. No one has been there. We learned it by studying how earthquake waves travel through the Earth.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 地球有四層。最外面是又薄又硬的地殼；底下是地函，很厚，是固體，卻能非常緩慢地流動；再往下是外核，是液態的鐵和鎳；最中心是內核，一顆固態的鐵球。沒有人去過那裡。我們是靠研究地震波怎麼穿過地球，才知道這些的。

tricks_head.en: The inside of the Earth in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住地球的內部

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. In “Layers,” move the slider or press “Go down” to travel from the surface to the center, and read what each layer is like. Then choose “Earthquake waves” to see how the waves from one earthquake cross the Earth, and where they cannot go.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。在「四層」的視角，拉動滑桿或按「往下走」，從地表一路走到地心，看看每一層是什麼樣子。再選「地震波」，看一個地震的波怎麼穿過地球，又有哪些地方到不了。

crust.en: The crust is the layer we live on. It is hard rock, anywhere from 5 to 70 kilometers thick and about 17 on average. Compared with the whole Earth, it is thinner than the skin on an apple. The deepest hole ever drilled stops at about 12 kilometers.
crust.zh: 地殼是我們住的這一層。它是堅硬的岩石，厚度從 5 公里到 70 公里不等，平均大約 17 公里。和整個地球比起來，它比蘋果的皮還薄。人類鑽過最深的洞，大約在 12 公里就停了。

mantle.en: The mantle is the thickest layer and makes up most of the Earth. It is solid rock, with temperatures of 2,000 to 3,000°C. Yet over a very long time it flows, slowly, and that slow flow helps move the plates above it.
mantle.zh: 地函是最厚的一層，地球大部分都是它。它是固態的岩石，溫度高達攝氏 2,000 到 3,000 度。可是時間拉得夠長，它會慢慢地流動；這種緩慢的流動，推著上面的板塊移動。

outer.en: The outer core is liquid: melted iron and nickel, about 2,220 kilometers thick. The moving metal makes the Earth's magnetic field, the one that turns a compass needle.
outer.zh: 外核是液體：熔化的鐵和鎳，大約有 2,220 公里厚。這些流動的金屬產生了地球的磁場，就是讓指南針轉動的那個磁場。

inner.en: The inner core is a solid ball of iron about 1,251 kilometers in radius. It is thousands of degrees hot, but the weight of the whole Earth presses on it so hard that the iron cannot melt.
inner.zh: 內核是一顆固態的鐵球，半徑大約 1,251 公里。這裡有好幾千度，可是整個地球的重量壓在它上面，壓力大到鐵沒辦法熔化。

lab.waves_en: An earthquake at the top sends waves through the whole Earth. S waves cannot travel through liquid, so they stop at the outer core. P waves get through, but the core bends them. That leaves a band on the far side, from 103 to 143 degrees away, where instruments record no direct P waves. This shadow zone told scientists that the Earth has a core, and that part of it is liquid.
lab.waves_zh: 頂端的地震把波送進整個地球。S 波沒辦法穿過液體，所以到外核就停了。P 波穿得過去，可是會被地核折彎。結果在地球的另一側，距離 103 度到 143 度之間，儀器收不到直接的 P 波。這個「陰影帶」讓科學家知道：地球有一個核心，而且其中一部分是液體。

legend.en: From the edge inward: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core
legend.zh: 由外到內：地殼、地函、外核、內核

legend.en: Lines: P waves (yellow) and S waves (red)
legend.zh: 線條：P 波（黃）與 S 波（紅）

lab.scale_en: The mantle, outer core, and inner core are drawn to scale, using the Central Weather Administration's figures. The crust is not: at its true size it would be thinner than a line on your screen, so it is drawn about ten times too thick. The paths of the earthquake waves are simplified, and the land and sea on the outside are only decoration.
lab.scale_zh: 地函、外核、內核是照中央氣象署的數字，依真實比例畫的。地殼不是：照真實比例，它會比螢幕上的一條線還細，所以畫厚了大約十倍。地震波的路徑是簡化過的；外面的陸地和海洋只是裝飾。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The figures follow the Central Weather Administration's “100 Questions About Earthquakes” and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；數字依中央氣象署「地震百問」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: How far down can people dig? The deepest hole ever drilled is in the far north of Russia. Scientists worked on it for many years, and in 1989 it reached 12,262 meters, a little more than 12 kilometers. That sounds deep. But the center of the Earth is 6,371 kilometers below your feet. The hole did not even get through the outer skin.

That outer skin is called the crust. It is the hard rock we live on, and it lies under the oceans too. The crust is from 5 to 70 kilometers thick, and about 17 kilometers on average. If the Earth were an apple, the crust would be thinner than the peel.

Below the crust is the mantle, the thickest layer by far. It reaches down to 2,900 kilometers and makes up more than four fifths of the Earth. The mantle is solid rock, and it is very hot: 2,000 to 3,000 degrees Celsius. Over millions of years it flows, very slowly, and this slow movement helps push the plates of the crust around.

Under the mantle is the core, and it has two parts. The outer core is a deep ocean of liquid iron and nickel. As this metal moves, it makes the Earth's magnetic field. At the very center is the inner core, a ball of iron about 1,251 kilometers in radius. It is even hotter than the outer core, yet it is solid, because the pressure there is so great.

But if no one has ever been deeper than 12 kilometers, how do we know any of this? The answer is earthquakes. Earthquake waves travel all the way through the Earth, and they change speed and direction when the rock changes. One kind, the S wave, cannot pass through liquid at all. By recording the waves all over the world, scientists can work out what lies below.

In 1909 a scientist named Andrija Mohorovičić found the bottom of the crust this way. In 1936 Inge Lehmann studied earthquake records and discovered that the core has a solid center. Every large earthquake still teaches us something. We have never seen the inside of our planet, but we have learned to listen to it.
paras_zh: 人類可以往下挖多深？世界上鑽過最深的洞在俄羅斯的極北地區。科學家花了很多年，1989 年鑽到 12,262 公尺，也就是 12 公里多一點。聽起來很深吧？可是地球的中心在你腳下 6,371 公里的地方。這個洞連最外面那層皮都還沒穿過去。
那層皮叫做地殼。它是我們居住的堅硬岩石，海洋底下也是地殼。地殼的厚度從 5 公里到 70 公里，平均大約 17 公里。如果把地球想成一顆蘋果，地殼比蘋果皮還要薄。
地殼底下是地函，它是最厚的一層，而且厚得多。它一路延伸到 2,900 公里深，占了地球的五分之四以上。地函是固態的岩石，而且非常熱：攝氏 2,000 到 3,000 度。經過幾百萬年，它會非常緩慢地流動；這種緩慢的移動，幫忙推著地殼的板塊到處跑。
地函底下是地核，分成兩個部分。外核是一片很深的液態鐵和鎳的海洋；這些金屬流動的時候，就產生了地球的磁場。最中心是內核，一顆半徑大約 1,251 公里的鐵球。它比外核還熱，卻是固體，因為那裡的壓力太大了。
可是，既然從來沒有人到過比 12 公里更深的地方，我們怎麼會知道這些？答案是地震。地震波會一路穿過地球，而且岩石一變，波的速度和方向就跟著變。其中一種叫 S 波，完全沒辦法穿過液體。科學家在世界各地記錄這些波，就能推算出底下有什麼。
1909 年，一位叫莫霍洛維奇的科學家就是用這個方法找到地殼的底部。1936 年，英厄．雷曼研究地震紀錄，發現地核的中心是固體。直到今天，每一次大地震都還在教我們新的東西。我們從來沒有親眼看過這顆行星的內部，但我們學會了怎麼聽它。
questions: What are the four layers of the Earth, from the outside in?
How is the outer core different from the inner core?
How do scientists know what is inside the Earth?
answers: The crust, the mantle, the outer core, and the inner core.
The outer core is liquid iron and nickel. The inner core is a solid ball of iron, kept solid by the great pressure.
They record earthquake waves all over the world. The waves change speed and direction in different kinds of rock, and S waves cannot pass through liquid.

vocab.ex: The mantle is the thickest layer of the Earth.
vocab.exzh: 地函是地球最厚的一層。

vocab.ex: Throw the apple core in the trash.
Ice is water in its solid form.
They drilled a hole in the wall.
vocab.exzh: 他們在牆上鑽了一個洞。

vocab.ex: Check the air pressure in the tires.

quiz.q: Which layer of the Earth is the thickest?
What is the outer core made of?
Why is the inner core solid even though it is so hot?
options: The pressure is too great for it to melt

quiz.q: How deep is the deepest hole people have drilled?
options: All the way to the center

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試
parts_head.en: Four stops on the way down

parts.text_en: Stop where the drill stopped. You are less than 0.2% of the way to the center.
parts.text_zh: 停在鑽頭停下來的地方。你走了到地心路程的 0.2% 都不到。

parts.text_en: Solid rock at thousands of degrees, flowing more slowly than you can imagine.
parts.text_zh: 幾千度的固態岩石，流動得比你想像的還要慢。

parts.text_en: A sea of melted metal. Its movement makes the Earth a giant magnet.
parts.text_zh: 一片熔化的金屬海。它的流動讓地球變成一塊巨大的磁鐵。

parts.text_en: Watch the red S waves stop at the liquid, and find the gray band where no direct P waves arrive.
parts.text_zh: 看紅色的 S 波在液體前停下來，再找找那一段收不到直接 P 波的灰色地帶。

lessons.parts_note_en: The depths of the layers follow the Central Weather Administration: the mantle ends at 2,900 kilometers, and the inner core begins at about 5,120.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 各層的深度依中央氣象署的數字：地函到 2,900 公里為止，內核大約從 5,120 公里開始。

links.k_zh: 地球與天氣 第二課
links.en: Why Does Taiwan Have So Many Earthquakes?
links.zh: 台灣為什麼地震這麼多？
links.note_en: The plates of the crust move, get stuck, and slip. Meet the P waves and S waves again.
links.note_zh: 地殼的板塊會移動、卡住、滑動。P 波和 S 波在這裡再登場一次。

links.k_zh: 地球與天氣 第五課
links.note_en: Sometimes rock from below melts and finds its way up.
links.note_zh: 有時候底下的岩石熔化了，就會找路往上跑。

dig.eyebrow: A Trip to the Center · 到地心的旅程
dig.lead_en: Nobody can really travel to the center of the Earth. But pretend you could go straight down at a steady speed. Choose a ride and see how long each layer takes. Notice how quickly you leave the crust behind.
dig.lead_zh: 沒有人真的能到地心去。不過假裝你可以用固定的速度一路往下：選一種交通工具，看看每一層要走多久。注意看，你多快就離開地殼了。
dig.note_en: The speeds are round examples: walking at 5 kilometers an hour, a car at 100, a fast train at 300, and a jet at 900. The distances are the thickness of each layer: 17, 2,883, 2,220, and 1,251 kilometers.
dig.note_zh: 速度是取整數的例子：走路每小時 5 公里、汽車 100、高速列車 300、噴射機 900。距離是每一層的厚度：17、2,883、2,220、1,251 公里。

facts.eyebrow: The Earth by the Numbers · 地球的數字
facts.en: Six numbers about the inside of the Earth
facts.zh: 六個和地球內部有關的數字
facts.lead_en: From the surface to the center.

items.en: The distance from the surface to the center of the Earth.
items.zh: 從地表到地球中心的距離。

items.en: The average thickness of the crust. It ranges from 5 to 70.
items.zh: 地殼的平均厚度；最薄 5 公里，最厚 70 公里。

items.en: The share of the Earth that is mantle.
items.zh: 地函占整個地球的比例。

items.en: The depth of the deepest hole ever drilled, reached in 1989.
items.zh: 人類鑽過最深的洞，1989 年鑽到的深度。

items.en: Near the surface, the rock gets about 1°C hotter for every 30 meters you go down.
items.zh: 在地表附近，每往下 30 公尺，岩石大約就熱攝氏 1 度。

items.en: The shadow zone: the band where no direct P waves from an earthquake arrive.
items.zh: 陰影帶：收不到地震直接傳來的 P 波的那一段。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories from Below · 來自地底的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A very deep hole, the bottom of the crust, a solid heart, and a planet that is a magnet
culture_cards.title_zh: 很深的洞、地殼的底、固態的中心，還有一顆會當磁鐵的行星
culture_cards.lead_en: Four discoveries about a place no one has visited.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個發現，說的是一個從來沒有人去過的地方。

cards.body_en: On the Kola Peninsula in Russia, scientists set out to drill as deep into the crust as they could. In 1979 their hole became the deepest in the world, and in 1989 it reached 12,262 meters. A later attempt had to stop when the rock turned out to be 180°C, much hotter than expected.
cards.body_zh: 在俄羅斯的科拉半島，科學家想盡可能往地殼深處鑽。1979 年，他們的洞成了全世界最深的；1989 年鑽到 12,262 公尺。後來再往下鑽的時候，發現岩石的溫度高達攝氏 180 度，比原先預期的熱得多，只好停下來。

cards.body_en: In 1909 the Croatian scientist Andrija Mohorovičić noticed something odd in his earthquake records: two sets of waves from the same earthquake. One set had come straight through the crust. The other had dipped down into faster rock and come back up. He had found the boundary between the crust and the mantle. It is still called the Moho.
cards.body_zh: 1909 年，克羅埃西亞的科學家莫霍洛維奇在地震紀錄裡發現一件怪事：同一個地震，竟然有兩組波。一組直接穿過地殼；另一組往下鑽進傳得比較快的岩層，再繞上來。他找到了地殼和地函的交界，到今天這個交界面還叫做「莫霍面」。

cards.body_en: Scientists once thought the whole core was liquid. Then the Danish scientist Inge Lehmann studied the records of earthquakes in New Zealand. Some waves seemed to bounce off something deep inside the core. In 1936 she showed that the liquid core has a solid center.
cards.body_zh: 科學家原本以為整個地核都是液體。後來，丹麥的科學家英厄．雷曼研究了紐西蘭地震的紀錄，發現有些波好像被地核深處的某個東西反彈回來。1936 年，她證明了液態的地核裡面有一個固態的中心。

cards.en: A planet that is a magnet
cards.body_en: Why does a compass needle point north? The answer is in the outer core. Heat escaping from the core keeps the liquid iron and nickel moving, and the moving metal carries electric currents. Those currents make the magnetic field that surrounds the whole Earth.
cards.body_zh: 指南針的針為什麼會指向北方？答案在外核。從地核往外散的熱，讓液態的鐵和鎳不停地流動，流動的金屬帶著電流，這些電流就產生了包住整個地球的磁場。

myths.myth_en: The inside of the Earth is all melted rock.
myths.myth_zh: 地球裡面全都是熔化的岩漿。
myths.fact_en: Most of it is solid. The mantle is solid rock and the inner core is solid iron. Only the outer core is liquid.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分是固體。地函是固態的岩石，內核是固態的鐵，只有外核是液體。

myths.myth_en: People have drilled deep into the Earth.
myths.myth_zh: 人類已經鑽到地球很深的地方了。
myths.fact_en: The deepest hole is about 12 kilometers, less than 0.2% of the way to the center.
myths.fact_zh: 最深的洞大約 12 公里，連到地心路程的 0.2% 都不到。

myths.myth_en: The center of the Earth is liquid because it is the hottest part.
myths.myth_zh: 地球的中心最熱，所以是液體。
myths.fact_en: It is the hottest part, but it is solid. The pressure is so great that the iron cannot melt.
myths.fact_zh: 那裡確實最熱，卻是固體。壓力太大了，鐵沒辦法熔化。

myths.myth_en: Scientists are only guessing about what is down there.
myths.myth_zh: 底下有什麼，科學家只是用猜的。
myths.fact_en: They measure it. Earthquake waves recorded all over the world show where the layers begin and end.
myths.fact_zh: 他們是量出來的。世界各地記錄到的地震波，顯示出每一層從哪裡開始、到哪裡結束。

tricks.body_en: Crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.
Only the outer core is liquid.
That is the crust we live on.

tricks.title_en: We listen, we do not look
tricks.body_zh: 地震波就是我們的眼睛。

safety.en: Ask an adult to cut the fruit or the egg. Do not use a sharp knife by yourself.
safety.zh: 切水果或水煮蛋請大人幫忙，不要自己用利刀。

safety.en: Wash your hands before and after you handle food, and do not eat anything that has been on the floor or the desk.
safety.zh: 碰食物前後都要洗手；掉在地上或放在桌面上的東西不要吃。

safety.en: Tell your teacher if you are allergic to any food before the activity begins.
safety.zh: 如果你對某些食物過敏，活動開始前先告訴老師。

materials.en: A hard-boiled egg for each group, and a plate
materials.zh: 每組一顆水煮蛋，還有一個盤子

materials.en: A ruler and a knife (for the adult)
materials.zh: 一把尺，還有一把刀（由大人使用）

steps.en: Tap the egg gently so that the shell cracks into several pieces but stays on. These pieces are your plates.
steps.zh: 輕輕敲蛋，讓蛋殼裂成好幾片但還留在蛋上。這幾片就是你的「板塊」。

steps.en: Ask the adult to cut the egg in half through the shell.
steps.zh: 請大人連殼把蛋切成兩半。

steps.en: Look at the cut face. Which part is like the crust, which the mantle, and which the core? Measure how thick each one is.
steps.zh: 看看切面。哪一部分像地殼？哪一部分像地函？哪一部分像地核？量量看每一層有多厚。

steps.en: Talk about it: in what ways is the egg a good model of the Earth? In what ways is it wrong?
steps.zh: 討論：這顆蛋有哪些地方很像地球？又有哪些地方不對？

activities.tip_en: One thing the egg gets wrong: the yolk is one piece, but the Earth's core has a liquid outer part and a solid center.
activities.tip_zh: 這顆蛋有一個地方不對：蛋黃是完整的一塊，可是地球的地核外面是液體、中心是固體。

materials.en: Several closed boxes or cans, each with something different inside: sand, a marble, water in a small sealed bottle, cotton
materials.zh: 幾個蓋好的盒子或罐子，裡面各放不同的東西：沙子、彈珠、裝在密封小瓶裡的水、棉花

steps.en: Do not open the boxes. Shake each one, tilt it, and tap it, and listen carefully.
steps.zh: 不可以打開盒子。把每一個搖一搖、歪一歪、敲一敲，仔細聽。

steps.en: Write down what you think is inside each box, and what clue made you think so.
steps.zh: 寫下你覺得每個盒子裡是什麼，以及是哪個線索讓你這麼想的。

steps.en: Is it solid or liquid? One piece or many? How can you tell without looking?
steps.zh: 它是固體還是液體？是一整塊還是很多小塊？不用看，你怎麼知道？

steps.en: Open the boxes and check. Which were easy? Which fooled you?
steps.zh: 打開盒子對答案。哪些很容易？哪些把你騙了？

activities.tip_en: This is how scientists study the Earth. They cannot open it, so they send waves through it and listen to what comes back.
activities.tip_zh: 科學家就是這樣研究地球的。他們沒辦法把地球打開，所以讓波穿過去，再聽傳回來的是什麼。

sources.en: The Earth's layers: crust 5 to 70 km thick, about 17 km on average; mantle down to 2,900 km, 83% of the Earth's volume, solid but able to flow slowly, its convection a cause of plate movement; core from 2,900 km to the center at 6,371 km; outer core about 2,220 km thick, liquid iron and nickel; inner core a solid iron ball 1,251 km in radius
sources.zh: 地球內部構造：地殼厚 5 至 70 公里，平均約 17 公里；地函至 2,900 公里，占總體積 83%，固體但能緩慢流動，對流是板塊運動的原因之一；地核自 2,900 公里至 6,371 公里的地心；外核厚約 2,220 公里，液態鐵鎳；內核是半徑 1,251 公里的固態鐵球
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 2

sources.en: Average thickness, mass, and volume of each layer
sources.zh: 各層的平均厚度、質量與體積
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 3

sources.en: Near the surface the temperature rises about 1°C for every 30 m; the mantle is at 2,000 to 3,000°C
sources.zh: 近地表平均每 30 公尺升高約 1°C；地函溫度 2,000 至 3,000°C
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 7

sources.en: The P wave shadow zone between 103° and 143°, evidence that the Earth has layers
sources.zh: P 波陰影帶在 103° 至 143° 之間，是地球內部分層的證據
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 24

sources.en: S waves are stopped at the liquid outer core; P waves are refracted
sources.zh: S 波在液態外核停住；P 波被折射
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Shadow zone”

sources.en: The Kola Superdeep Borehole: the deepest human-made hole since 1979; 12,262 m reached in 1989; later drilling stopped at higher-than-expected temperatures of 180°C
sources.zh: 科拉超深鑽孔：1979 年起為最深的人造鑽孔；1989 年達 12,262 公尺；後續鑽探因溫度高於預期（180°C）而停止
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Kola Superdeep Borehole”

sources.en: The Mohorovičić discontinuity, first identified in 1909 by Andrija Mohorovičić from two sets of waves on seismograms
sources.zh: 莫霍面：1909 年由 Andrija Mohorovičić 從地震圖上的兩組波辨認出來
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Mohorovičić discontinuity”

sources.en: The solid inner core, discovered in 1936 by Inge Lehmann from seismograms of earthquakes in New Zealand; the inner core is solid because of its high pressure
sources.zh: 固態內核：1936 年由 Inge Lehmann 研究紐西蘭地震的地震圖發現；內核因高壓而呈固態
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Earth's inner core”

sources.en: The magnetic field is generated by electric currents from the motion of molten iron and nickel in the outer core, driven by heat escaping from the core
sources.zh: 地球磁場由外核中熔融鐵鎳流動產生的電流所形成，流動的動力來自地核散出的熱
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Earth's magnetic field”

lessons.title: Why Does Taiwan Have So Many Earthquakes?
lessons.title_zh: 台灣為什麼地震這麼多？
lessons.blurb_en: Taiwan records about 40,000 earthquakes a year, and people can feel about 1,000 of them. Why here? In a 3D model, watch one plate push against another until a stuck fault suddenly slips. Then find out why your phone can ring a few seconds before the shaking starts.
lessons.blurb_zh: 台灣每年大約測到四萬次地震，其中人感覺得到的大約有一千次。為什麼偏偏是這裡？在 3D 模型裡，看一塊板塊推著另一塊，直到卡住的斷層突然滑動。再來看看，手機為什麼能在開始搖之前幾秒就響起來。
lessons.big_idea_en: The Earth's surface is made of huge plates that move a few centimeters a year. Taiwan sits where two of them meet, and one pushes hard against the other. The rock gets stuck, bends, and stores up force. When it can hold no more, it slips all at once. That sudden slip is an earthquake.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 地球的表面是由幾塊巨大的板塊組成的，每年移動幾公分。台灣剛好在兩塊板塊相接的地方，其中一塊用力推著另一塊。岩層卡住、被壓彎，把力存了起來；到了撐不住的時候，就一下子滑動。這突然的一滑，就是地震。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. This is a slice of the Earth's crust. The right side is pushed toward the left, but the sloping fault between them is stuck. Watch the rock bend and turn red as the force builds, and watch what happens when the fault gives way. Then choose a fault that is stuck harder and compare.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。這是切開的一塊地殼。右邊一直被往左推，可是中間那條斜的斷層卡住了。看岩層怎麼被壓彎、隨著力的累積變紅，再看斷層撐不住的時候會發生什麼事。接著選一條卡得比較緊的斷層，比一比。

build-easy.en: The plate keeps pushing, but the fault does not move. The rock is squeezed like a spring. This fault lets go fairly easily, so the force never builds very high.
build-easy.zh: 板塊一直在推，斷層卻不動，岩層像彈簧一樣被壓縮。這條斷層比較容易放手，所以力不會累積得太高。

build-hard.en: This fault is stuck hard, so it holds on much longer. Look how much the rock bends and how far the land rises before anything happens.
build-hard.zh: 這條斷層卡得很緊，所以撐得久得多。看看在出事之前，岩層彎了多少、地面隆起了多少。

quake-easy.en: The fault slips, and the stored force goes out as waves. The yellow ring is the P wave, which is fast. The red ring is the S wave, which is slower but shakes harder. This was a smaller earthquake.
quake-easy.zh: 斷層滑動了，存起來的力變成波傳出去。黃色的圈是 P 波，跑得快；紅色的圈是 S 波，慢一點，可是搖得比較厲害。這是一次比較小的地震。

quake-hard.en: After a long wait, the fault slips a long way all at once. The more force that was stored, the bigger the earthquake. Watch the far house: the P wave reaches it first, and the strong S wave comes after.
quake-hard.zh: 等了很久之後，斷層一次滑了很長一段。存的力越多，地震就越大。注意遠處那間房子：P 波先到，強烈的 S 波後到。

legend.en: Rings: P wave (yellow) and S wave (red)
legend.zh: 圓圈：P 波（黃）與 S 波（紅）

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not to scale. The push of 7.5 centimeters a year follows the Central Weather Administration's figure of 7 to 8, but everything else is an example: real faults do not slip on a regular schedule, the plate's movement is shared among many faults, and the bending and slipping here are drawn hundreds of times too large so that you can see them. During the earthquake the model switches to slow motion.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型，不是真實比例。每年推 7.5 公分是照中央氣象署「每年約 7 至 8 公分」的數字，其他都是示例：真的斷層不會這麼規律地滑動，板塊的移動也是由很多條斷層一起分擔的；為了讓你看得見，岩層的彎曲和滑動都畫大了好幾百倍。地震發生的那一刻，模型會改成慢動作。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the Central Weather Administration's “100 Questions About Earthquakes” and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依中央氣象署「地震百問」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Your phone makes a loud sound. A few seconds later, the lamp begins to swing and the floor moves under your feet. If you live in Taiwan, you know this feeling well. Taiwan records about 40,000 earthquakes every year. Most are too small to notice, but people can feel about 1,000 of them. Why does the ground here shake so often?

The answer begins with the Earth's outer shell. It is not one piece. It is broken into huge slabs of rock called plates, and the plates move very slowly, a few centimeters a year. Taiwan sits right where two plates meet: the Eurasian Plate and the Philippine Sea Plate. The Philippine Sea Plate pushes toward the northwest at about 7 to 8 centimeters a year.

If the plates slid past each other smoothly, we would feel nothing. But rock is rough, and the plates get stuck along cracks called faults. The plate keeps pushing while the fault stays stuck, so the rock bends, a little like a plastic ruler. All that time, it is storing up force. At last the rock can hold no more. The fault slips suddenly, and the rock springs back. That is an earthquake.

The slip sends out waves through the ground. The fastest ones, called P waves, arrive first and usually shake gently. The S waves come next, and they shake harder. Instruments near the earthquake catch the first waves, and computers quickly send an alert. For places far enough away, the alert can arrive seconds, or even tens of seconds, before the strong shaking.

Most of Taiwan's earthquakes happen in the east, where the two plates meet. Yet earthquakes in the west often do more damage. They tend to be shallow, they happen under the land, and many people live there. A strong earthquake under a crowded plain is more dangerous than a stronger one far out at sea.

Can scientists tell us when the next big one will come? Not yet. No one can predict the time, place, and size of an earthquake. What we can do is be ready. When the ground shakes, drop down, take cover under a strong table, and hold on. The same push that shakes Taiwan also built its high mountains. Earthquakes are part of living on a young, growing island.
paras_zh: 手機發出很大的聲音。幾秒鐘之後，燈開始晃，腳下的地板也動了起來。住在台灣的人，對這種感覺再熟悉不過。台灣每年大約測到四萬次地震，大部分小到沒有人注意，但其中大約有一千次是人感覺得到的。這裡的地為什麼這麼常搖？
答案要從地球的外殼說起。它不是完整的一塊，而是裂成好幾片巨大的岩石板，叫做板塊。板塊移動得非常慢，每年只有幾公分。台灣剛好在兩塊板塊相接的地方：歐亞板塊和菲律賓海板塊。菲律賓海板塊每年大約以 7 到 8 公分的速度往西北方推擠。
如果板塊之間可以順順地滑過去，我們什麼都感覺不到。可是岩石很粗糙，板塊會沿著叫做「斷層」的裂縫卡住。板塊繼續推，斷層卻卡著不動，岩層就被壓彎了，有點像一把被折彎的塑膠尺。這段時間裡，它一直在把力存起來。最後岩層撐不住了，斷層突然滑動，岩層彈了回去。這就是地震。
這一滑，會把波從地底送出去。跑得最快的叫做 P 波，最先到，通常搖得比較輕。接著來的是 S 波，搖得比較厲害。地震附近的儀器收到最早的波，電腦很快算出結果、發出警報。對離得夠遠的地方來說，警報可以比強烈的搖晃早幾秒、甚至幾十秒到。
台灣的地震大部分發生在東部，也就是兩塊板塊相接的地方。可是西部的地震常常造成比較大的災害：它們通常比較淺、發生在陸地底下，而且那裡住了很多人。一個發生在擁擠平原底下的強震，比遠在外海、規模更大的地震還要危險。
科學家能不能告訴我們下一次大地震什麼時候來？現在還不行。沒有人能預測地震發生的時間、地點和大小。我們能做的是準備好。地開始搖的時候：趴下、躲到堅固的桌子底下掩護、穩住。推著台灣搖晃的這股力量，也把台灣的高山推了起來。住在一座年輕、還在長大的島上，地震就是生活的一部分。
questions: Which two plates meet at Taiwan?
What happens along a fault before and during an earthquake?
Why can an earthquake alert arrive before the strong shaking?
answers: The Eurasian Plate and the Philippine Sea Plate.
Before the earthquake, the plate keeps pushing but the fault is stuck, so the rock bends and stores up force. During the earthquake, the fault slips suddenly and the rock springs back.
Instruments near the earthquake catch the first waves, and the alert is sent out very quickly. In places far enough away, it arrives before the slower, stronger S waves do.

vocab.ex: The earthquake woke everyone up last night.
vocab.exzh: 昨晚的地震把大家都搖醒了。
台灣位在兩塊板塊相接的地方。
岩層沿著一條斷層裂開。

vocab.ex: The drawer is stuck. I cannot open it.
Be careful not to slip on the wet floor.
vocab.exzh: 小心不要在濕地板上滑倒。

vocab.ex: The windows shake when a truck goes by.
vocab.exzh: 卡車經過的時候窗戶會搖。
我的手機跳出地震警報。

quiz.q: What happens when a stuck fault finally gives way?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_zh: 在這個模型裡每 40 年一次
parts.text_en: The force never builds very high. The earthquakes are smaller, but there are more of them.
parts.text_zh: 力累積得不高。地震比較小，可是次數比較多。

parts.en: A fault that is stuck hard
parts.meta_zh: 在這個模型裡每 160 年一次
parts.text_en: A long, quiet wait, and then a very large slip. Quiet does not mean safe.
parts.text_zh: 安靜地等了很久，然後一次滑很大一段。安靜不代表安全。

parts.meta_zh: P 波先到，S 波後到
parts.text_en: Jump to the moment just before the slip. Watch the yellow ring race ahead of the red one.
parts.text_zh: 直接跳到滑動前的那一刻。看黃色的圈怎麼跑在紅色的圈前面。

parts.text_en: Run the whole story again and watch the land on the right. Each slip lifts it a little higher.
parts.text_zh: 從頭再看一次，注意右邊的地面。每滑一次，它就被抬高一點。

lessons.parts_note_en: The 40 and 160 years are examples. Real faults do not keep a schedule, which is one reason earthquakes cannot be predicted.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 40 年和 160 年只是例子。真的斷層不會照時間表來，這也是地震沒辦法預測的原因之一。

links_head.en: The same push, two more stories
links_head.zh: 同一股推力的另外兩個故事

links.en: How Does GPS Know Where You Are?
links.zh: GPS 怎麼知道你在哪裡？
links.note_en: Scientists use satellite positioning to measure how the ground slowly moves and bends.
links.note_zh: 科學家就是用衛星定位，量出地面怎麼慢慢移動、變形。

links.k_zh: 地球與天氣 第四課
links.note_en: The push that causes earthquakes also lifts the land.
links.note_zh: 造成地震的那股推力，也把地面往上抬。

warn.eyebrow: The Earthquake Alert · 地震警報
warn.en: How many seconds do you get?
warn.lead_en: An earthquake alert is not a prediction. The earthquake has already begun, and the alert is racing the waves to reach you. Move the slider to change how far you are from the earthquake, and see who wins the race.
warn.lead_zh: 地震警報不是預測。地震已經發生了，警報是在和地震波賽跑，看誰先到你這裡。拉動滑桿改變你離地震的距離，看看誰贏。
warn.note_en: An example with round numbers: P waves at 7 kilometers a second, S waves at 4, and an alert sent 19 seconds after the earthquake begins. The Central Weather Administration says it needs about 15 to 20 seconds to work out where the earthquake is and 1 to 2 more to send the alert. Real waves change speed with the rock and the depth, so real warning times differ.
warn.note_zh: 這是用整數做的例子：P 波每秒 7 公里、S 波每秒 4 公里，地震發生後 19 秒發出警報。中央氣象署表示，大約需要 15 到 20 秒算出地震的位置，再用 1 到 2 秒發出警報。真的地震波速度會隨著岩層和深度改變，所以實際的預警時間會不一樣。

facts.eyebrow: Taiwan's Earthquakes by the Numbers · 台灣地震的數字
facts.en: Six numbers from the Central Weather Administration
facts.zh: 中央氣象署的六個數字
facts.lead_en: All six come from the agency that measures Taiwan's earthquakes.
facts.lead_zh: 這六個數字都來自負責測量台灣地震的機關。

items.en: About how many earthquakes Taiwan's instruments record in an ordinary year.
items.zh: 平常的年份，台灣的儀器一年大約測到這麼多次地震。

items.en: About how many of them are strong enough for people to feel.
items.zh: 其中大約有這麼多次，強到人感覺得到。

items.en: How fast the Philippine Sea Plate pushes toward the northwest against the Eurasian Plate.
items.zh: 菲律賓海板塊往西北方推擠歐亞板塊的速度。

items.en: About how long it takes, after an earthquake on or near the island begins, to work out where it is.
items.zh: 島內或近岸發生地震之後，大約要這麼久才能算出它的位置。

items.en: Each step up in magnitude means about 32 times more energy. Two steps means about 1,000 times.
items.zh: 規模每增加 1，能量大約多 32 倍；增加 2，大約是 1,000 倍。

items.en: The most earthquakes recorded in one year, because of the great earthquake of September 21 and those that followed.
items.zh: 單一年份測到最多次的紀錄，原因是九二一大地震和它之後的許多地震。

culture_cards.title_en: A bent fence line, a night in 1999, a ring around the ocean, and forty-nine seconds
culture_cards.title_zh: 被扯彎的地面、1999 年的一個夜晚、繞著海洋的一圈，還有四十九秒
culture_cards.lead_en: Four stories about how we came to understand earthquakes.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個故事，說的是我們怎麼慢慢弄懂地震。

cards.body_en: After the great San Francisco earthquake of 1906, the American scientist Harry Fielding Reid studied how the ground along a fault had moved in the fifty years before it. He saw that the land had been slowly bending the whole time. His idea, that rock stores force and then springs back, is called elastic rebound. It is still the main way we explain earthquakes.
cards.body_zh: 1906 年舊金山大地震之後，美國科學家李德研究了斷層兩邊的地面在地震前五十年是怎麼移動的。他發現，這段時間裡地面一直在慢慢彎曲。他的想法是：岩層先把力存起來，再彈回去。這叫做「彈性回彈」，到今天仍然是解釋地震最主要的理論。

cards.zh: 九月二十一日凌晨 1 點 47 分
cards.body_en: The Chi-Chi earthquake of 1999 was caused by the Chelungpu Fault in central Taiwan. The ground broke along a line about 100 kilometers long. In some places one side moved as much as 7 meters sideways and 4 meters up. September 21 is now National Disaster Prevention Day, and on that morning phones across Taiwan receive a practice alert.
cards.body_zh: 1999 年的集集大地震是車籠埔斷層引起的。地表沿著一條大約 100 公里長的線裂開，有些地方兩側水平錯開最多 7 公尺、垂直最多 4 公尺。現在，9 月 21 日是國家防災日，那天早上全台灣的手機都會收到一則演練用的警報。

cards.body_en: If you mark the world's earthquakes on a map, most of them fall along narrow bands. The biggest band runs all the way around the Pacific Ocean: through Japan, the Ryukyu Islands, Taiwan, the Philippines, and Indonesia to New Zealand, and down the west coasts of North and South America. About 90 percent of the world's earthquakes happen along it.
cards.body_zh: 把全世界的地震標在地圖上，會發現它們大多排成一條條細長的帶子。最大的一條繞了太平洋一整圈：經過日本、琉球、台灣、菲律賓、印尼到紐西蘭，再沿著南北美洲的西岸往下。全世界大約 90% 的地震發生在這一圈上。

cards.body_en: On February 6, 2016, an earthquake struck Meinong in southern Taiwan. About 12 seconds after it began, the Central Weather Administration's system had worked out where it was. For Taipei, far to the north, that meant 49 seconds of warning before the strong shaking arrived. Close to the earthquake, though, there was no time at all.
cards.body_zh: 2016 年 2 月 6 日，南台灣的美濃發生地震。地震發生後大約 12 秒，中央氣象署的系統就算出了它的位置。對遠在北邊的台北來說，這代表在強烈搖晃到達之前，有 49 秒的預警時間。不過在離地震很近的地方，一點時間都沒有。

myths.myth_en: Scientists can tell us when the next big earthquake will come.
myths.myth_zh: 科學家可以告訴我們下一次大地震什麼時候來。
myths.fact_en: Not yet. No one can predict the time, place, and size of an earthquake. That is why being ready matters.
myths.fact_zh: 現在還不行。沒有人能預測地震發生的時間、地點和大小。所以平常就要做好準備。

myths.myth_en: Strange clouds or hot, still weather mean an earthquake is coming.
myths.myth_zh: 出現奇怪的雲，或天氣又悶又熱，就是要地震了。
myths.fact_en: There is no evidence that weather and earthquakes are linked. So-called earthquake clouds are ordinary clouds, and earthquakes start deep underground.
myths.fact_zh: 沒有證據顯示天氣和地震有關。所謂的「地震雲」只是普通的雲，而地震是從很深的地底開始的。

myths.myth_en: The alert on my phone predicts the earthquake.
myths.myth_zh: 手機的警報是在預測地震。
myths.fact_en: The earthquake has already started. The alert simply travels faster than the strong waves.
myths.fact_zh: 地震已經發生了。警報只是跑得比強烈的地震波快。

myths.myth_en: A place with many small earthquakes is safe from big ones.
myths.myth_zh: 常常有小地震的地方，就不會有大地震。
myths.fact_en: Not so. A big earthquake can still happen there. Each step up in magnitude releases about 32 times more energy, so small ones cannot use it all up.
myths.fact_zh: 不是這樣。那裡還是可能發生大地震。規模每增加 1，放出的能量大約多 32 倍，小地震沒辦法把力全部用掉。

tricks.body_en: The Philippine Sea Plate pushes against the Eurasian Plate.
tricks.body_zh: 菲律賓海板塊推著歐亞板塊。

tricks.body_en: The rock stores force, then lets it go all at once.
tricks.body_zh: 岩層把力存起來，再一次放掉。

tricks.title_zh: P 波先到，S 波後到
tricks.body_en: The first wave is the gentle one. The strong one follows.
tricks.body_zh: 先到的搖得輕，後到的搖得重。

tricks.body_en: Do not wait to see how big it is.

safety_head.en: What to do when the ground shakes
safety_head.src: National Fire Agency, Fire Prevention and Disaster Education Hall
safety_head.src_en: These points follow Taiwan's official guidance:
safety_head.src_zh: 以上要點依內政部消防署「消防防災館」與中央氣象署「地震百問」的官方說明。

safety.en: The most important thing is to protect your head and neck. At once, drop down, take cover, and hold on.
safety.zh: 最重要的是保護頭部和頸部。馬上趴下、掩護、穩住。

safety.en: Get under a strong table and hold on to its leg. If the table moves, move with it.
safety.zh: 躲到堅固的桌子底下，握住桌腳。桌子移動的話，人跟著桌子一起移動。

safety.en: If you shelter beside a pillar or in a corner instead, watch out for furniture, lights, bookcases, and anything else that could fall.
safety.zh: 如果是躲在柱子旁邊或牆角，要小心家具、燈具、書櫃和其他可能掉下來的東西。

safety.en: Stay away from sea walls, riverbanks, and cliffs. If you live near the coast, move to high ground in case of a tsunami.
safety.zh: 遠離海堤、河堤和山崖。住在海邊的人要往高處移動，以防海嘯。

materials.en: A heavy book, a long rubber band, and a paper clip or string to hook the band to the book
materials.zh: 一本厚重的書、一條長橡皮筋，還有把橡皮筋勾在書上的迴紋針或線

materials.en: A rough table or a sheet of sandpaper, and a ruler
materials.zh: 粗糙的桌面或一張砂紙，還有一把尺

steps.en: Put the book on the rough surface and hook the rubber band to it.
steps.zh: 把書放在粗糙的面上，橡皮筋勾在書上。

steps.en: Pull the free end of the rubber band very slowly and steadily. Watch the band stretch while the book stays still.
steps.zh: 非常慢、非常穩地拉橡皮筋的另一頭。看橡皮筋越拉越長，書卻沒有動。

steps.en: Keep pulling until the book suddenly jumps. Measure how far it moved, then keep going and count the jumps.
steps.zh: 繼續拉，直到書突然往前一跳。量量看它移動了多遠，再繼續拉，數一數跳了幾次。

steps.en: Put a second book on top and try again. Are the jumps bigger or smaller? Do they come more often or less often?
steps.zh: 上面再疊一本書，重做一次。每次跳得比較遠還是比較近？跳得比較常還是比較少？

activities.tip_en: Your hand is the plate, the rubber band is the bending rock, and the jump is the earthquake. Could you tell exactly when each jump would happen?
activities.tip_zh: 你的手是板塊，橡皮筋是被壓彎的岩層，書跳的那一下就是地震。你有辦法準確說出每一次什麼時候跳嗎？

materials.en: Eight or more students standing in a line, each with hands on the shoulders of the person in front
materials.zh: 八位以上的同學排成一排，每個人把手搭在前面同學的肩膀上

materials.en: A timer, and a desk for each student to practice under afterward
materials.zh: 計時器；之後每人還需要一張可以躲的桌子

steps.en: P wave: the last student gently pushes forward and pulls back. Watch the push travel down the line.
steps.zh: P 波：最後一位同學輕輕往前推、再拉回來。看這一下怎麼沿著隊伍傳下去。

steps.en: S wave: the last student sways gently from side to side. Watch the sway travel down the line.
steps.zh: S 波：最後一位同學輕輕左右搖。看搖晃怎麼沿著隊伍傳下去。

steps.en: Time both waves from one end to the other. Which one was faster?
steps.zh: 兩種波都從頭計時到尾。哪一種比較快？

steps.en: Now the drill. When the teacher calls “Alert!”, everyone has ten seconds to drop, take cover under a desk, and hold on.
steps.zh: 接著演練。老師喊「警報！」的時候，每個人有十秒鐘趴下、躲到桌子底下掩護、穩住。

activities.tip_en: Push and sway gently, and keep your feet still. In the ground, the push wave really is the faster one, so your line of students should show the same thing.
activities.tip_zh: 推和搖都要輕輕的，腳不要移動。在地底下，「推」的那種波確實跑得比較快，你們的隊伍應該也會看到一樣的結果。

sources.en: Taiwan records about 40,000 earthquakes in an ordinary year, about 1,000 of them felt; the record of 49,928 in 1999
sources.zh: 臺灣常態年均測報約 40,000 次地震，其中有感約 1,000 次；1999 年 49,928 次為歷史最大值
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 54

sources.en: Taiwan lies on the boundary of the Eurasian Plate and the Philippine Sea Plate; the Philippine Sea Plate pushes northwest at about 7 to 8 centimeters a year; why the east has the most earthquakes
sources.zh: 臺灣位在歐亞板塊與菲律賓海板塊交界；菲律賓海板塊每年約 7 至 8 公分向西北擠壓；東部地震最多的原因
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 56

sources.en: Plate tectonics: the lithosphere is divided into plates that move a few centimeters a year relative to one another; most earthquakes happen where plates meet
sources.zh: 板塊構造：岩石圈分成數個板塊，彼此每年以數公分的相對速度移動；大部分地震發生在板塊交界
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 51

sources.en: Elastic rebound theory (Harry Fielding Reid): stress builds and the rock deforms, the rock breaks and slips, and the energy is released as it springs back
sources.zh: 彈性回彈理論（李德）：應力累積、岩層變形，超過極限時破裂位移，回彈時釋放能量
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 10

sources.en: Reid studied ground movement along the San Andreas Fault in the 50 years before the 1906 San Francisco earthquake
sources.zh: 李德研究 1906 年舊金山大地震前 50 年聖安地列斯斷層沿線的地表位移
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Elastic-rebound theory”

sources.en: P waves are the fastest and arrive first; S waves are next and usually more destructive
sources.zh: P 波速度最快、最先抵達；S 波次之，破壞力通常大於 P 波
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 21

sources.en: Typical P wave speeds in earthquakes are 5 to 8 km/s; P waves travel about 1.7 times as fast as S waves (basis for the example speeds of 7 and 4 km/s)
sources.zh: 地震 P 波速度一般為每秒 5 至 8 公里；P 波約為 S 波的 1.7 倍（示例取 7 與 4 km/s 的依據）
sources.src: Wikipedia, “P wave” and “Earthquake”

sources.en: Earthquake early warning: about 15 to 20 seconds to work out the location and 1 to 2 seconds to send it; several to tens of seconds of warning beyond 100 km; the 2016 Meinong earthquake (12 seconds, and 49 seconds of warning for Taipei)
sources.zh: 強震即時警報：約 15 至 20 秒算出震央、1 至 2 秒對外通報；100 公里以外有數秒至數十秒預警；2016 年美濃地震（12 秒算出，台北有 49 秒）
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 84

sources.en: Why earthquakes in the west do more damage: shallow, under land, and in crowded areas
sources.zh: 西部地震災害較嚴重的原因：震源淺、多在陸地、人口密集
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 57

sources.en: The time, place, and size of an earthquake cannot yet be predicted accurately
sources.zh: 目前尚無法以科學方式準確預測地震發生的時間、位置及規模
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 82

sources.en: No evidence links earthquakes to weather or seasons; “earthquake clouds” are ordinary clouds
sources.zh: 沒有證據顯示地震與天氣或季節有關；「地震雲」是常見的雲
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 55

sources.en: A place with frequent small earthquakes can still have a large one
sources.zh: 常有微小地震的地方仍可能發生大地震
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 78

sources.en: Each step of 1 in magnitude is about 32 times the energy; a step of 2 is about 1,000 times
sources.zh: 規模每增加 1，能量約 32 倍；增加 2，約 1,000 倍
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 29

sources.en: The Chi-Chi earthquake: September 21, 1999, 1:47 a.m.; Chelungpu Fault; a surface rupture about 100 km long; up to 7 m of horizontal and 4 m of vertical movement
sources.zh: 集集大地震：1999 年 9 月 21 日 1 時 47 分；車籠埔斷層；地表破裂帶長約 100 公里；水平位移最大 7 公尺、垂直最大 4 公尺
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 70

sources.en: September 21 is National Disaster Prevention Day; a drill message is sent to mobile phones that morning
sources.zh: 9 月 21 日為國家防災日；當天上午對手機發送演練訊息
sources.src: Wikipedia, “1999 Jiji earthquake”

sources.en: The belt of earthquakes around the Pacific and the places it passes through
sources.zh: 環太平洋地震帶與它經過的地方
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 52

sources.en: About 90% of the world's earthquakes occur along the Ring of Fire
sources.zh: 全世界約 90% 的地震發生在環太平洋火環上
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Ring of Fire” (citing the USGS)

sources.en: Protect your head and neck; drop, cover, and hold on; hold the table leg and move with the table; watch for furniture, lights, and bookcases
sources.zh: 保護頭部、頸部；趴下、掩護、穩住；握住桌腳、隨桌子移動；小心家具、燈具、書櫃
sources.src: 內政部消防署 消防防災館「地震了！該怎麼辦？」

sources.en: Do not shelter near riverbanks, sea walls, or cliffs; coastal residents should move to high ground
sources.zh: 不可躲在河、海堤或山崖附近；沿海居民應疏遷至高地以防海嘯
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 96
